title: GetAccept customers saw twice the 24-hour signing rate with SMS and email on the first reminder
summary: What gets documents signed? GetAccept data from thousands of closed documents: text reminders, video and comments each linked to higher signing rates.
body_markdown:
GetAccept’s signing reminder logs show that 25.9% of recipients signed within 24 hours of a first reminder by SMS and email, compared with 12.4% after email alone. GetAccept counted reminders sent at least 24 hours after the document went out.


**GetAccept research · November 2026**


## **Most texts went out on the third reminder or later**


After the second reminder, about 8% signed within a day in either group. On the third reminder or later, that figure was below 4% in both groups.


Companies that sent more reminders carry more weight in the chart. GetAccept also compared the two groups within each company. For the first reminder, the median gap was


**11 percentage points** in favor of text and email.


## **Documents sent with a text were signed more often in the examples**


These comparisons cover documents that were signed or closed without a signature. For each feature, GetAccept compared signing rates with and without it at the same company. Each figure below is the median of those differences across the examples.


### **Text at the original send**


The signing rate was


**13.6 percentage points higher** at the median when teams also sent the document by text. In every example, signed documents came back sooner on average when teams used a text. The examples covered 3,305 closed documents.


### **Video in the document**


The median signing rate gap was


**24.5 percentage points** in favor of documents with a video. This comparison covered 7,173 closed documents and included intro videos and videos added inside the document.


### **Comments on the document**


The median gap was


**about 46 percentage points** in favor of documents with a comment, across 17,278 closed documents. Buyers and sellers could both leave comments. Buyers who were already close to signing may have been more likely to comment.


## **Test text and email on the first reminder**


Pick a set of comparable unsigned documents that have been out for the same amount of time. Send an email to one group and an email plus a text to the other. Compare the share of recipients who sign within the next 24 hours.


In GetAccept, you can


[send a text reminder from the document](https://help.getaccept.com/en/articles/6294568-document-view) when the recipient has a mobile number on file.


## **How we counted signatures**


GetAccept numbered reminders separately for each recipient and document. A company needed at least 100 reminders by text and email and 100 by email alone at a given reminder number to count in that comparison.


The feature comparisons cover documents sent October 1, 2025 to September 28, 2026. Each company needed at least 30 closed documents with the feature and 30 without it.


A document can appear in more than one feature comparison. Teams chose which channels and features to use, so differences between buyers or deals can also account for part of the gap.
